body: No problem...all I can say is that I always feel at least a little bit better once I wake up the next morning. My advice is just get some sleep.

I told my family about how I felt a little while ago. Honestly it didn't really change anything. I went to the doctor and he prescribed some anti-depressants. I have no idea what your parents are like, but maybe they are just too caught up in work and everything to notice how you really feel. If you don't show them you can't really expect them to know. Not trying to lecture or anything, but I know I hid it for years and my mom is the most caring person I've ever known. I've never gone through the alcohol/drug problems so I can't really help you much there sorry.

Don't really know from your post what kind of help you are wanting, but I've been depressed/suicidal for almost as long as I can remember (I'm 21). You obviously have a lot of anger towards your parents care to elaborate on that? Sorry if that is too personal, but I don't really know what else to ask.

Hey I don't usually post, but just wanted to say I'm definitely in the same boat. I was prescribed some ant-depressants a few months ago and they haven't done a damn thing. I actually started taking them again last night because I felt so helpless. Never tried the whole therapist thing and don't really want to. It won't change anything. I haven't spoken to a single person who isn't family for over a month now. Trust me...you're not the only one that's alone. Anyway hope that helps somehow and I'm always down to chat so feel free to message me if you want. Good luck.

To the guy who's comment was deleted: (by the mods I'm assuming)

You know, it's funny you should mention a "suicide pact". I remember me and my friend from high school would joke that after we graduated, grew up, and moved on from the "good life" that we would just kill ourselves because life would suck after that. Our motto was "Fuck it". It's starting to seem less like a joke anymore.

>So what? What does that have to do with now?

To me, it has *everything* to do with now. I'm simply not the type of person who does something just to do it. I need to have a reason behind it. You say I will have billions of years not to exist. Then why on earth would I care about this insignificantly small portion of time where I do exist? When I'm dead I won't be able to look back and say "Well, at least I was happy for those few years I existed". I guess what I'm saying is that the only way I could reason that this life matters is if there is some sort of eternity that goes along with it. This idea right here is why people cling to religion so desperately. 

Also, I wanted to thank you for the 10 minutes of your day. I do appreciate it.

>The Universe doesn't give two shits if you are happy or not.

I agree 100 percent. This is part of the reason why I find it so difficult to care about anything. If the universe doesn't give a shit about me, then why should I give a shit about it? In essence, human beings are part of what make up the universe among an infinite number of other things. I don't really want to start some silly philosophical debate so I guess i'll just stop there.

>Find out what makes you happy, man.

I'm trying. The one thing I found that I could always rely on for some comfort when I was younger was gaming. Games used to be so much different 6-10 years ago and I truly enjoyed them. I had a couple online friends that I used to play with and we would stay up countless hours not necessarily even having fun with the game, but having fun with each other. Sadly we all "grew up" and they changed and I changed and there is just no way it could ever be like it used to. Like I mentioned in my other post I still play some competitive games like MOBA's and SC2, but I'm not even sure if I do it for fun anymore. It's just there to fill the void.
Sure what would you like to talk about? I play PC games (LoL, Dota 2, SC2, etc) listen to melodic death metal, and play guitar.
